title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
A Tesla vehicle operating under Autopilot was involved in a fatal crash. Tesla told the family of the deceased that data from the vehicle's systems about the crash was unavailable. A hacker later demonstrated that such data is routinely retained by Tesla vehicles, contradicting the company's assertion to the family.

This is a failure to disclose data that existed in the system. The failure occurred at the point of communicating with the crash victim's family and persisted through litigation. It would have been caught by basic verification that the vehicle retained the data it claimed to lack, or by disclosure protocols that required checking what information was actually available before making statements about its absence.

A jury found Tesla liable and awarded more than $240 million in damages. A judge upheld this verdict. Whether Tesla's initial statement about missing data reflected a genuine error in locating the records or a deliberate misrepresentation is not established by the reporting.
